content.value_statement: Teams often copy Helm examples that do not match their operational constraints. This skill guides chart architecture through dependencies, hooks, values, environments, and operator needs.
actual_capabilities: Guides component and dependency decisions for Helm chart architecture.
Evaluates when to use subcharts, external services, or independent charts.
Reviews lifecycle hooks for idempotence, safety, and operational value.
Designs values.yaml as an operator-facing configuration contract.
Plans multi-environment chart behavior for dev, staging, and production.
Identifies extensibility points such as sidecars, annotations, and extra volumes.
limitations: Does not generate a complete chart without project-specific requirements.
Does not validate live clusters or run Helm commands by itself.
Does not replace security review of rendered Kubernetes manifests.
Depends on accurate input about teams, dependencies, and environments.

use_cases.title: Design a New Service Chart
use_cases.description: Create a chart architecture for a microservice with clear dependencies, values, hooks, and environment behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Patterns
use_cases.description: Define library chart boundaries, security defaults, and reusable templates for many application teams.

use_cases.title: Review Chart Maintainability
use_cases.description: Assess whether an existing chart is extensible, understandable, and ready for production operations.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Chart Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new application chart.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Helm Chart Architect skill to design a Helm chart for my application. Ask me for missing requirements before proposing architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Dependency Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request about managed services and subcharts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Helm Chart Architect skill to compare subcharts, external services, and independent charts for my dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Review Lifecycle Hooks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for install, upgrade, and test behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Helm Chart Architect skill to review lifecycle hooks for migrations, validation, smoke tests, and deletion behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Enterprise Chart Governance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multi-team platform standards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Helm Chart Architect skill to design chart governance across platform, application, DevOps, and security teams.

output_examples.input: A team needs a Helm chart for a FastAPI service with PostgreSQL, Redis, and separate production requirements.
output: A component map that separates critical services, optional services, and external dependencies.
A dependency strategy that uses local subcharts in development and managed services in production.
A values design that exposes replicas, resources, external endpoints, and extension points.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants reusable Helm patterns for several application teams.
output: A recommendation to separate library charts from application charts.
Clear ownership boundaries for platform defaults, application logic, and environment values.
A review checklist for security context, probes, labels, and operator documentation.

output_examples.input: An existing chart has complex hooks and confusing values.
output: A hook review focused on idempotence, failure behavior, and deletion policies.
A simplified values contract that removes unclear options and documents important decisions.
Operational checks that help users diagnose failed installs and upgrades.

best_practices: Provide project requirements, dependency ownership, and environment differences before asking for architecture.
Review the proposed values contract with the operators who will deploy the chart.
Validate recommendations with Helm lint, schema checks, and rendered manifest review.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a generic chart template without explaining operational constraints.
Do not expose every internal chart detail as a values option.
Do not rely on hooks that fail when they run more than once.

faq.question: Does this skill create Helm chart files?
faq.answer: It focuses on architecture decisions first. It can guide chart structure, but complete files need project details.

faq.question: Can it help with existing charts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review chart coupling, values design, hooks, dependencies, and operator experience.

faq.question: Does it require access to my Kubernetes cluster?
faq.answer: No. The skill reasons from requirements and chart content. It does not inspect live clusters.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide components, dependencies, environments, team ownership, security rules, and known operational failures.

faq.question: Can it support AI or GPU workloads?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes an example for LLM fine-tuning, GPU scheduling, queues, and training parameters.

faq.question: How should I verify its recommendations?
faq.answer: Use Helm lint, values schema validation, rendered manifest review, and operational smoke tests.
